intro: This clinic mixes every compound verb. The first verb is given; you choose the second, and each second verb carries one image: 込む in, 出す out or suddenly starting, 上げる / 上がる up or finished, 切る to the end, 合う each other, 直す again to fix, 返す back, かける towards or half-done. Do not translate the English phrasal verb word by word: name the image, then pick the verb.

skills.rule: First recall the fixed words, then ask in order: direction (in, out, up)? a sudden start? done to the end? each other? again or back? aimed at someone or half-done?
skills.explain:
Step 1, fixed words. Some compounds are words to know whole: 思い出す (remember), 出かける (go out), 間に合う (be in time), 付き合う (go out with), 申し込む (apply), 落ち込む (feel down), 繰り返す (repeat), 出来上がる (be ready).

Step 2, direction. Into, inside, deeply: 込む (飛び込む). Out, emerging: 出す (取り出す). Up: 上げる when you lift something (持ち上げる), 上がる when the subject rises (立ち上がる).

Step 3, a sudden start that carries on (rain, tears, running): 出す (降り出す).

Step 4, completion. Nothing left, or 'cannot finish it all': 切る / 切れない. A finished piece of work: 上げる / 上がる (書き上げる, 出来上がる).

Step 5, two people doing it to each other: 合う.

Step 6, again. To fix a bad first try: 直す. Back to a person, an owner or the start: 返す.

Step 7, aimed at someone (with に), or begun and stopped: かける.
patterns: in → 込む; out → 出す; up → 上げる (transitive) / 上がる (intransitive)
sudden start → 出す; begun and stopped, or aimed at someone → かける
nothing left → 切る; finished product → 上げる
each other → 合う; redo to fix → 直す; back / repeat → 返す

examples.jp: 子供[こども]が急[きゅう]に道[みち]に{飛[と]び出[だ]して}きた。
examples.en: A child suddenly ran out into the road.

examples.jp: 夏[なつ]は毎日[まいにち]プールに{飛[と]び込[こ]みます}。
examples.en: In summer I dive into the pool every day.

examples.jp: 電車[でんしゃ]で隣[となり]の人[ひと]に{話[はな]しかけた}。
examples.en: On the train I started talking to the person next to me.

examples.jp: 二人[ふたり]でこれからのことを{話[はな]し合[あ]った}。
examples.en: The two of us talked over what to do from now on.

examples.jp: 一晩[ひとばん]でレポートを{書[か]き上[あ]げた}。
examples.en: I finished writing the report in a single night.

examples.jp: 先生[せんせい]に言[い]われて、レポートを{書[か]き直[なお]した}。
examples.en: The teacher told me to, so I rewrote the report.

contrast.note: Opposite directions: 飛び込む (dive in) and 飛び出す (rush out); 持ち込む (bring in) and 持ち出す (take out).
Both finish. 使い切る: consumed until none is left. 書き上げる: worked until a finished piece exists.

contrast.vs: かける / 合う / 込む
contrast.note: With 話す: 話しかける, start talking to someone; 話し合う, discuss together; 話し込む, talk at length, absorbed.

mistakes.bad: 急[きゅう]に雨[あめ]が{降[ふ]り込[こ]んだ}ので、傘[かさ]を買[か]った。
mistakes.good: 急[きゅう]に雨[あめ]が{降[ふ]り出[だ]した}ので、傘[かさ]を買[か]った。
mistakes.note: Rain suddenly starting is 出す; 降り込む means rain blowing in through a window.

mistakes.bad: 名前[なまえ]を呼[よ]ばれて、{立[た]ち上[あ]げた}。
mistakes.good: 名前[なまえ]を呼[よ]ばれて、{立[た]ち上[あ]がった}。
mistakes.note: You stand yourself up: intransitive 上がる. 上げる needs an object (パソコンを立ち上げる).

mistakes.bad: 失敗[しっぱい]したので、最初[さいしょ]から{やり返[かえ]した}。
mistakes.good: 失敗[しっぱい]したので、最初[さいしょ]から{やり直[なお]した}。
mistakes.note: Redoing to fix is 直す; やり返す means getting even.

skills.tip: Say the image in one English word (in, out, up, all, together, again, back, at) before you look at the options.
